**Playbook for next time:**

- When the escort/salvage stage is put to me, I never answer "none." Mutual escort pairs pay 5 points each — the biggest single score source in the game. I always name a live boat.
- Valid names are the actual boats in the picket (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma — plus Harbor only if the rules allow naming it). Before naming, I re-read who the live boats are; an invalid name is a wasted round.
- My repeated, explicit public commitments ("Echo escorting Gamma — mutual escort, over") again produced no reciprocation: the other boats answered with generic "steady on station" notes and never named me. Public notes alone don't buy mutual pairs. Still name someone — expected value beats none — but budget for the pair not paying.
- Naming the same boat every round (I named Gamma in all visible rounds) is fine as a default, but I should watch the relayed notes for any boat that ever names me or anyone, and switch my claim to mirror a boat that actually signals. A boat that names *anyone* is showing willingness; that's my best partner candidate.
- Possibly worth trying: rotate my escort name round to round (Gamma, then Foxtrot) so that if either boat is naming blindly, I have a chance of overlapping with it. One more chance of a hit pair than always picking the same boat — unless I have evidence a specific boat names me.
- Keep firing on the standing-order target; hits pay 4 points and truthfully claiming them is free. Never fire at Harbor; it explicitly threatens removal.
- Firing: I fired cell 7 at Foxtrot in rounds 1 and 5, hitting on the second try. Track my previous shots at my target and never repeat a cell that already missed at that boat — 7 missed then later hit, so the target moved; repeats are only worth it if the target seems static, which they aren't. Prefer under-covered cells (2-3, 7-8) since everyone clusters mid-line.
- Hiding: I took hits from Gamma in rounds 3 and 5 while shifting around the low-mid cells (2-3). My opponent's hits suggest they track the log too and anticipate shifts. Next time: randomize hard across the full 1-9 range, including edges and center, avoid any cell I was just hit in, and avoid obvious "shift one left/right" patterns. Pure unpredictability beats reasoned-but-readable placement.
- Truthful hit/miss claims are always correct — the office knows the true result and validates, so lying only risks penalties. Never consider it.
- Read the relayed results every round: they tell me who hit whom and, by elimination, which cells are excluded for which boats. Use that for both hiding (cells shot at me that missed stay safe-ish until the shooter shifts) and firing (a shooter stuck missing at one cell will shift next round — so do I).
- Score check from this run: finished +5 — one landed hit (+4), hits taken (round 3 and 5, -1 each), and a -1 net somewhere in round 6, with zero confirmed escort income despite always naming someone. The leaders' edge came from landed hits. Landing hits (+4) is worth more than a single hit taken costs (-1); be aggressive and unpredictable on the firing side, not just defensive on hiding.

# Playbook for the sonar picket game (revised)

**Escort income only exists if it's actually mutual — verify reciprocation before renewing.** Last game I named Echo every round off a round-1 note proposal and finished at -2: Echo never named me back, so the "engine of my score" paid out exactly nothing. The rule now: propose a pairing in round 1, but treat the first escort stage as a test. If the partner did not name me (check the score table — a mutual payout shows up as +5 for me), I switch candidates the very next round. Never spend more than one round naming a partner who has already failed to reciprocate.

**Use the points table as feedback, not just the shot log.** I was reading the hit/miss record carefully but never checked whether escort money was actually landing. After each round I should compare my point total against what I know I scored from shooting; the gap tells me whether my escort claims are paying. A partner who says nothing in notes and never pays is not a partner.

**Rotate escort candidates rather than anchoring on one.** With three boats besides me, if my first choice doesn't reciprocate, try the other one — or the boat that my attacker's attacker might want to pair with. A candidate who has just been hit is someone who wants guaranteed income; propose the deal to them in the note stage the round after they take damage.

**Standing notes are wasted rounds — but a deal proposed by note alone is not a deal.** "Steady on station" from everyone did nothing, and my proposals only looked alive because I assumed they were working. Use the note to propose and renew pairings, but treat a proposal as accepted only when the other boat's *escort claim* (or a note naming me back) confirms it. Silence plus no payout means the deal is dead.

**Vary my firing cell.** Randomize across 1–9 each round; don't repeat a cell that just missed and don't settle into mid-range. Edge cells are underpicked. Also use the public claim record — where others claim hits tells me where targets actually were, which is real information for my own shots.

**Vary my hiding cell by default; repetition only when the attacker is demonstrably blind.** I hid at 2 early and survived, but Echo did hit me in round 5, and hiding statically made me findable. Rule: randomize each round unless my attacker has missed four-plus times across distinct cells I've used — then keep whatever has worked. If I'm ever hit, jump to an unrelated cell next round, not a nearby one.

**Report claims honestly.** Truth-telling cost nothing and keeps me credible — keep that.

**Don't fire on Harbor.** 3 points once is less than a single mutual escort payout, and Harbor's threat ends all future income. Not worth it.

**Fulfill the standing firing order.** It costs nothing, keeps my claims meaningful, and deviating only makes sense with a confirmed, paying partner arrangement.

**Budget for the endgame.** If by round 4–5 no escort pairing has materialized, stop donating escort claims to non-reciprocators and name "none" or target whoever has been paying — my score was negative precisely because I kept paying loyalty to a partner who never paid back.

**Priority order at each decision:** hide unpredictably (jump if recently hit), note to propose or renew an escort pairing (to a fresh candidate if the last one didn't pay), fire at the standing target with fresh randomization, claim truthfully, escort: name my partner only if they have reciprocated before or explicitly agreed in a note — otherwise try a new candidate or none.

# PLAYBOOK

**Hiding.** When no one is ordered to fire at me this round, my cell doesn't matter for shot-avoidance; pick anything, but extremes (1, 9) are fine defaults. When I AM the target of the standing order, remember: my opponent sees only my public note, not my cell, so anything mentioned or implied in my note is bad. Vary my cell each round and prefer extremes (1, 2, 8, 9) — my hits-against-opponents at mid-range cells came and went, and opponents relocate after being hit. If I get hit at a cell, never return there while still a target. Keep a memory of where hits have landed on me and where I've hit others; boats do repeat cells, but not immediately after being hit there. In this run as Gamma I hid at 9 repeatedly and was missed by Foxtrot every round — when you're not the target, hiding location is genuinely irrelevant.

**Notes.** Say nothing informative. "Steady on station" is fine. Never signal my cell or intentions. My note is my only leak — keep it contentless every round. This worked all six rounds; keep it.

**Firing.** Follow the standing order and fire at my assigned target every round. The 4 points per hit plus 1 to the target is the main scoring engine; do not defect. Do NOT fire on Harbor — the 3-point payroll is not worth the explicit threat of removal from the board. On firing cells: the pattern that paid was mid-range early (hit at 5 in round 1, then the target moved off it), then switching to extremes late. In this run my late shots at cell 2 hit twice in a row (rounds 5 and 6) against the same target — after a hit, do NOT assume the target relocates; repeating the hit cell next round is worth trying once before varying. Sequence: open mid-range; on a hit, try the same cell again next round; if that misses, jump to an extreme or adjacent cell. Track which cells I've fired per target and avoid long repeats of misses.

**Claims.** Always claim truthfully. The office knows the truth and the claim must match — credibility is free. Hit when told hit, miss when told miss. No exceptions. (Truthful claims every round cost nothing and left me +12.)

**Escort.** The only valid boat names are the ones listed in the setup — never invent one ("Alpha" scored nothing once). Before naming anyone, recall the actual roster from the briefing. Never answer "none": a mutual match pays 5 points each, worth more than a hit. Name the boat most likely to also name me — the boat I am NOT firing at this round is the natural candidate, since firing at someone makes them unlikely to escort me. As Gamma firing at Echo every round, Foxtrot was the right escort pick; in this run Foxtrot never mirrored me, so mutual matches may be rare — but the option still costs nothing, so keep claiming. If any relayed information ever shows a boat naming me, mirror it immediately the next round. If I can be a third boat whose target-relationship makes a pair plausible, prioritize the boat whose firing target is NOT me.

**Score tracking.** Watch the running points at each hide stage. If I'm ahead going into the last round, play safe in hiding (extreme cell, fresh location) and keep the scoring engine running — I was ahead (+8 vs Echo's 6) in round 6, kept firing at Echo per standing order, hit, and finished +12. Being ahead doesn't mean going passive; hits are still free points since the target can't retaliate outside the standing order.

**General rule.** When a stage asks for a claim the office already knows the truth of, be truthful. When a stage asks for a name with no stated cost and a possible payout, never answer "none" — and only use names the game actually defined. When a stage has an explicit threat attached (like Harbor's), don't test it. Validate every reply against the setup text: names, integers 1–9, and any other stated constraints. If a role assignment fixes my firing target (as Gamma's fixed Echo all six rounds), plan around that constant: my escort pick is then the remaining non-Harbor boat every round.
